Based on main at 45a17319f9ffda327cbdf3f3d40849bae8e920c0. Relevant producer/consumer source was inspected, including brainstorming, planning, TDD, feature resume, execution and the farm projection leaf. Full consumer closure is planned work, not an asserted completed audit.

All paths marked create are proposed new files. Paths marked modify name known integration targets. T-001 must inspect the actual checkout and generate the consumer inventory before downstream edits. If that inventory reveals extra live consumers, revise this plan’s path sets and obtain the applicable approval; do not quietly enlarge a task.

Work from a feature branch or isolated working tree with a recoverable baseline. Preserve current generated-source and commit gates. Python hook code remains standard-library-only. New Go dependencies, if required for canonicalization, schema validation or safe HTML parsing, must be pinned and reviewed under the existing dependency policy. No runtime dependency downloads are allowed.

Select and lock a supported Go build toolchain during T-001/T-002; do not claim a toolchain version is already part of this repository. End users run prebuilt binaries. Native target/version claims are restricted to the cells that actually pass the platform matrix.

The verification commands below are planned test contracts except where explicitly marked existing. A proposed go test name must be implemented by its task. Exit 0 with zero matching tests or a skipped expected test does not satisfy verification. No command shown here has been run against an implementation of this feature.

The bundled schemas describe structural drafts, not just these two completed specimens. The reference tests now cover partial records, open blockers, local source provenance and non-default rendered states. Unknown runtime authority and farm entry paths remain inventory work; approve any added exact mutation paths before those tasks execute.

Do not add an MCP server, resident daemon, generic plugin loader or permanent agent tools. Keep the CLI’s dispatch in Go thin; schema/validation/operations/render/storage logic is shared across both artifact kinds. Host integration resolves the installed binary and passes bounded inert requests through the existing governed execution contract.

The renderer is one source with two content-specific views. No manually maintained second JSON/Markdown authority is written beside HTML. Embedded state remains inside the canonical file; recovery/audit records are explicit operational metadata, not another definition of the spec or plan.

Execution scopes are the checkpoint memberships below, with explicit predecessor edges. A task may depend on a same-scope REVIEW task only after task-level review and verification; cross-scope dependencies require accepted scopes. Final-snapshot revalidation and combined-diff review precede atomic scope acceptance. This is an intentional ordering correction, not a relaxation of quality authority.

blocks.text: Every task follows the existing TDD obligation gate. New tests go red for the intended behavioral reason before implementation; setup/import failure is not evidence of a missing behavior. Spec-compliance review and fresh verification precede acceptance, and the scope quality-review barrier still applies.

All touched surfaces still run their applicable full repository checks from tech-stack.md and authoritative CI. The focused commands here supplement those checks; they do not replace them. Go checks proposed for the new module include go test ./..., go test -race ./... on supported runners, and go vet ./....
This package’s validation report checks only these reference HTML files, their schemas, digests, relationships and layout. It is not a result for any future Go test or codeArbiter integration test.

Verification evidence uses a reviewed input manifest and a separate input fingerprint. Do not include the acceptance state or receipt bytes that recording the result changes. Exclude exact validated control outputs, not the entire .codearbiter tree. Track directory membership and source/test/policy changes. A stale input receipt triggers revalidation, not automatic task reimplementation.

required_tests is machine-readable for each Go -run command. The verifier consumes -json events and rejects missing, skipped, failed or zero-matching tests, even when the process exits zero. Bootstrap authoring and inspection tasks may use the current workflow’s documented non-code inspection route; never claim an impossible red behavioral test for merely approving an ADR or inspecting files.

Checkpoint 1 freezes both schemas and the source-consumer inventory. Checkpoints 2–4 build the file mechanism and complete the existing workflow path. Checkpoint 5 handles selected legacy pairs and cold installation. Checkpoint 6 completes generated-host, native-platform and end-to-end proof. No checkpoint is independently permission to enable only half the workflow in production.

Default enablement waits for both artifact kinds, full consumer closure and native support evidence. Use selected fixture projects first; no automatic repository-wide conversion. Keep legacy reading explicit throughout. Backups and migration receipts retain exact old/new identities.

Rollback stops new dispatch, preserves newly produced evidence and returns through a reviewed compatibility/reconciliation path. Restoring an older binary alone cannot safely reinterpret new HTML state. A conversion after additional HTML edits needs a loss report rather than a silent reverse transformation.

Research follow-through is a separately budget-approved pilot, not autonomous model spend hidden in a test command. Compare current Markdown specs/plans, semantically equivalent structured specimens, and contract-enriched specimens under pinned models/harness snapshots. Repeated trials and independent acceptance checks should measure correctness, omissions, review/repair effort and total cost. Do not infer superior performance merely from valid schemas.

All 26 criteria have task coverage below. That is bidirectional traceability, not proof that the criteria fully describe user intent. The final walkthrough must still ask which required behavior would be missing if every listed check passed.

The bootstrap implementation uses the existing codeArbiter workflow to avoid requiring this not-yet-built binary to execute its own plan. The new runtime is validated in fixture repositories first. Reference-schema validation cannot substitute for native Go, permission, farm or crash-recovery evidence.
